row.scim_plan: Enterprise Pro (50+ seats, contract) or Enterprise Max
row.evidence: Perplexity's pricing table marks "Integrate with your identity provider for SCIM" as "Contract required" on Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max, and the help centre says SCIM is exclusive to Enterprise organizations with 50 seats or more, or with at least one Enterprise Max user.
row.notes: New row. Enterprise Pro ($34/seat/mo annual) includes SAML SSO; SCIM needs a sales contract and either 50+ seats or one Enterprise Max seat ($271/seat/mo annual), so it is priced as Contact Sales with a 50-seat minimum. Billing FAQ lists $40/mo or $400/yr for Pro and $325/mo or $3,250/yr for Max (the $34 and $271 headline prices are annual equivalents). SSO and SCIM run through WorkOS; IdPs offered in setup are Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace and Custom SCIM. Okta setup uses a custom SAML app with SCIM API integration (no OIN app found). SCIM deactivation removes the user from the org and frees the seat. Roles are mapped from two IdP groups (Admin/Member). JIT on SSO sign-in is an optional toggle. Audit logs (50+ seats or Enterprise Max) are pushed to a webhook. No user-management API; the public API only has org usage analytics.

plans.name: Enterprise Pro
plans.price_text: $34/seat/month billed annually ($40 monthly, $400/year per billing FAQ)
plans.notes: SCIM and audit logs on Enterprise Pro need 50+ seats and a contract ("Contract required").

plans.name: Enterprise Max
plans.price_text: $271/seat/month billed annually ($325 monthly, $3,250/year per billing FAQ)
plans.notes: Pricing table still marks SCIM "Contract required"; help centre says one Enterprise Max seat unlocks SCIM.

scim.plan: Enterprise Pro with 50+ seats (contract) or any org with an Enterprise Max seat

auth.token_source: Settings > Organization > Identity > SCIM > Connect (IdP-specific setup steps, run through WorkOS)

endpoints.notes: Inferred from the documented Custom SCIM option and SCIM-synced groups; Perplexity does not publish a SCIM endpoint reference.

deprovision.notes: Users deactivated in the IdP are removed from the organization; removing a member frees the seat for reassignment but does not reduce the purchased seat count.

roles.how: Group-to-role mapping: map one IdP group to the Admin role and one to the Member role in the SCIM role-assignment settings.

limitations.text: SCIM requires 50+ seats or at least one Enterprise Max seat; the pricing page marks SCIM as "Contract required".
SCIM-managed user records cannot be edited or removed in the Perplexity UI.
No welcome e-mail is sent to SCIM-provisioned users.
Users who already belong to another Perplexity organization are excluded from the SCIM sync.
SCIM article says user groups are not supported beyond Admin/Member; the newer Roles & Permissions article describes read-only SCIM-synced groups that depend on plan.
Domains must be verified before SCIM can be enabled.

webhooks_user_events.notes: Delivered as audit-log events to a customer webhook.

audit_log_api.plan: Enterprise with 50+ seats or an Enterprise Max seat
audit_log_api.notes: Push delivery to a customer-configured HTTPS webhook, not a pull API.

limitations.text: The public API documents an org-scoped Analytics API (usage per member) but no user, group or seat management endpoints.

okta.notes: Help centre has Okta set up as a custom SAML 2.0 app with SCIM provisioning enabled on it; no Okta Integration Network page found.

entra.notes: Entra ID listed in the SCIM setup picker; no Entra gallery tutorial found.

google.notes: Google Workspace listed in the SCIM setup picker; mechanism not documented.

conflicts.text: SCIM article says Perplexity user groups are not supported beyond Admin and Member, while the Roles & Permissions article describes read-only SCIM-synced groups (plan-dependent).
Pricing page shows Enterprise Pro at $34 and Max at $271 per seat per month billed annually; billing FAQ gives $400 and $3,250 per year ($33.33 and $270.83 per month).
SSO Getting Started says users must be invited to sign in with SSO, while the SSO troubleshooting article documents an optional JIT provisioning toggle.
